composing_text: 29th Armoured Brigade; 159th Infantry Brigade; UK-ARM-004B (for Operation Epsom)
notes: Landed about 13 June (Wikipedia list shows Juno).

current_activity: reaching ridge south of Cheux; engaged by 12th SS
notes: Armoured reconnaissance reached ridge south of Cheux 14:30, engaged by 12th SS Panzer IVs; division lost 21 tanks on 26 June.
Odon bridge at Tourmauville seized 27 June; 159th Brigade crossed the Odon on foot by night to reinforce the bridgehead.

notes: 23rd Hussars with infantry advanced on Hill 112, securing the northern slope but unable to take the reverse slope; 12th SS counter-attacks; division lost nearly 40 tanks on its slopes by end of day and was surrounded on three sides; infantry took Baron-sur-Odon.

current_activity: withdrawing 29th Armoured Brigade north of the Odon
notes: Dempsey withdrew the 29th Armoured Brigade north across the Odon after dark on 29 June to meet the expected German offensive; 159th Brigade placed under 15th Division command; II SS Panzer Corps counter-attack of 29 June largely spent by nightfall.

current_activity: Goodwood: leads VIII Corps from Escoville; the 29th Armoured Brigade is pinned down south of the railway
notes: Event date: 18 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 340, 342). Event definition: The division starts from just south of the minefield belt between Escoville and Ste. Honorine behind a barrage of some 200 guns, the 29th Armoured Brigade on the left and the 159th Brigade on the right, and advances well at first; by midday only the two armoured regiments of the 29th Brigade are south of the second railway and they are virtually pinned down (pp. 340 and 342). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 340: "the 11th Armoured Division started from just south of the mincfield belt between Escoville and Ste. Honorine"; p. 342: "The two armoured regiments of 29th Armoured Brigade, alone south of the railway, suffered heavily as they tried to fight their way up the slopes and by midday were virtually pinned down". Location: Escoville, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Escoville, the village at the start line; the division advanced south from it during the day. Location support: Ellis names the start line between Escoville and Ste. Honorine (p. 340).

current_activity: Bluecoat: advances on the right of the 15th Division towards St. Martin-des-Besaces and is ordered to continue at night
notes: Event date: 30 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 388, 392). Event definition: The division begins its advance a few minutes before 07:00 on the right of the 15th Division; by dusk its leading troops are about a mile past Dampierre and the 29th Brigade has taken St. Jean-des-Essartiers, two miles short of St. Martin, and it is ordered to continue into the night (pp. 388, 390 and 392). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 388: "11th Armoured Division was meanwhile to make good the area round St. Martin des Besaces"; p. 392: "But 11th Armoured Division had orders to continue the advance into the night". Location: Saint-Martin-des-Besaces, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 5 km. Location approximate: the point is St. Martin-des-Besaces, the objective; the division was two miles short of it at dusk. Location support: Ellis names St. Martin des Besaces as the objective (p. 388).

current_activity: Bluecoat: armoured cars find the Souleuvre bridge intact; the division crosses and holds a bridgehead at Le Beny-Bocage
notes: Event date: 31 July 1944 (Ellis, vol. I, pp. 393, 394). Event definition: A squadron of the Household Cavalry armoured cars reports at 10:35 that the bridge over the Souleuvre, five miles behind the German front, is clear of the enemy and intact; tanks make it secure, and the division pushes troops across that night and forms a bridgehead on the hills west of Le Beny-Bocage, with the slopes of Point 205 occupied (pp. 393-394); Le Beny-Bocage itself is taken on 1 August (p. 394). Event support: one source family (Ellis, the British official history). Ellis, Victory in the West, vol. I, p. 393: "Next morning the 21st Panzer Division made several attempts to assemble"; p. 394: "enabled 11th Armoured Division to push troops across the river that night and reach the hills west of le Bény- Bocage; a good bridgehead was formed and the slopes of Point 205 occupied". Location: Le Bény-Bocage, Calvados (new place) with a precision of 3 km. Location approximate: the point is Le Beny-Bocage, the town beside the bridgehead; the bridge itself is about two miles to the west. Location support: Ellis names the Souleuvre bridge two miles west of Le Beny-Bocage and the hills west of the town (p. 394).
